officer.label: Company Officer / Acting Officer
officer.summary: Manage the whole problem: size-up, strategy, crew deployment, risk, communication, accountability and development.
guide: Size-up
Occupancy, construction, conditions, life hazard, access, resources, water and initial assignments.
Coordination
Match tasks to strategy and monitor how actions affect one another.
Leadership
Set expectations, coach, document appropriately and develop members.
Risk/accountability
Crew location/function, changing conditions, PAR, rehab and Mayday response.
Development
Balance training, education, relevant experience and continuing education.
cards: What changes as officer?
You own crew safety, communication, coordination, development and decision consequences.
Useful initial size-up?
Concise building/occupancy, conditions, life hazard, actions, needs and command.
When should strategy change?
When risk/benefit, conditions, resources or progress no longer support it.
Strong assignment?
Clear task, location, objective and communication path.
USFA development pillars?
Training, academic education, relevant experience and continuing education.
quiz: Crew finishes assignment as conditions change.
Reassess, communicate progress/needs and align next action with strategy
Promotional plan built only on certs is incomplete because:
Education, experience and CE also matter
Current USFA development guidance integrates all four pillars.
next: Run tabletop size-ups with another officer.
Lead a drill tied to a real gap.

instructor.label: Instructor / Training Role
instructor.summary: Teach for job transfer: observable objectives, correct demonstration, repetitions, decision practice, evaluation and training safety.
guide: Objectives
Describe observable learner behavior, conditions and performance.
Skill teaching
Explain, demonstrate, guide practice, allow repetitions, give feedback and re-test.
Scenarios
Reveal information when learners take actions; allow safe mistakes and debrief reasoning.
Evaluation
Use clear criteria and separate safety-critical failures from coaching points.
Safety/documentation
Risk controls, rehab/emergency plan, attendance, remediation and lessons learned.
cards: Measurable objective?
An observable learner action rather than a vague word like understand.
Progressive disclosure?
Information appears after the learner takes an appropriate action to discover it.
Why allow wrong decisions in training?
Safe failure plus debrief can expose reasoning gaps.
Strong debrief question?
What were you seeing, what did it mean, and what would make you change the plan?
Best skill feedback?
Specific observation, standard/impact and another corrected repetition.
quiz: Scenario gives hidden fire location automatically.
Decision training is stronger when learners gather information.
Training objectives never override immediate safety controls.
